label: Augustine, De civitate Dei VIII.6: the Platonist philosophers, reasoning that bodies and minds…
paraphrase: Augustine, De civitate Dei VIII.6: the Platonist philosophers, reasoning that bodies and minds admit more and less of beauty and so are changeable, saw that there is an unchangeable first form and rightly believed it the principle of things, made by nothing and by which all things were made; so God showed them what is known of him, since they understood his invisible things through the things that are made (Rom 1:19-20).
